seller.role_title: Hospital front desk and intake coordinator

card.field: Hospital front desk intake and insurance verification
card.one_liner: Eligibility screens that lie, referral expiry, and when a 15-minute no-show rule should bend.

rules.text: Verify insurance at check-in for every visit, not only new patients.
A specialist referral is valid for 90 days or 3 visits, whichever ends first.
New patients go only into 30-minute slots; follow-ups into 15-minute slots.
Collect the copay before the visit unless the plan shows a 0 dollar copay.

exceptions.text: If the last visit was over 60 days ago, call the payer line; the eligibility screen lags by up to 30 days.
Government-plan eligibility is real-time, so the 60-day call rule does not apply to those patients.
Dermatology and OB allow self-referral on 12 of our plans; keep the one-page list because the screen does not show it.
Prior authorization for imaging can be requested same-day if the ordering physician marks it urgent; the normal path is 5 business days.

judgment_calls.text: At 15 minutes late, check the phone log and the lab queue before releasing the slot; hold up to 25 minutes if either shows the patient.
A walk-in with chest discomfort who refuses the ER over cost goes to the free triage room, not to an argument.
When the eligibility screen shows a plan that terminated under 30 days ago, treat the patient as self-pay pending and do not bill the old plan.

common_mistakes.text: Releasing the slot at exactly 15 minutes, charging a 50 dollar no-show fee the patient will dispute.
Booking a specialist visit without a referral on file, which produces a 400 dollar bill to the patient.
Trusting the eligibility screen for a patient last seen 6 months ago; the denied claim costs about 180 dollars in rework.

never_do.text: Never book a referral-required specialist visit without the referral; refuse and book a nurse triage call instead.
Never argue cost with a chest-pain walk-in; route to triage within 10 minutes.
Never put a new patient in a 15-minute slot to fill a gap.
